summon.text: The Brain of Cthulhu spawns upon destroying every third Crimson Heart in a Crimson world. It can also be summoned manually by using a Bloody Spine in The Crimson or Underground Crimson, at any time.

prepChecklist.text: Set up rows of platforms across the Chasm's central chamber and light it up
Block off the entrances of nearby chambers so enemies can't enter
Place Peace Candles or drink a Calming Potion before the fight
Using a Bloody Spine: keep a surface arena low so you stay in the Crimson
Drink Ironskin, Swiftness and Regeneration Potions
Equip a Cloud in a Bottle for a double jump
Wear Hermes Boots for speed
Carry a stack of the best healing potion you have

strategies.text: Brain of Cthulhu has 2 phases, with the latter starting after all Creepers have been dealt with.
Jump out of the way, either by using your platforms or with an extra jump, then attack the Creepers. Use piercing weapons to speed up the process.
Creepers have low individual health and are especially susceptible to the On Fire! and Frostburn debuffs.

When all of the Creepers are dead, the Brain will split, revealing a Heart with an Eye on the inside. The Brain teleports much more frequently, often at unexpected angles, and will try to ram into you.
If you have a weapon with high knockback, it will excel at dealing with the Brain, so much so that it's possible to stand in one location and attack it whenever it gets close.
During the second phase, the Brain will spawn clones of itself around the player.
Life-draining debuffs such as On Fire! and Frostburn will help distinguish them. Additionally, summoned minions and sentries will always target the correct copy.
The real Brain is the only one with a health bar.
A spear is a good weapon against the Brain of Cthulhu during the second stage.
A flail of some kind is beneficial for taking out the Creepers; the easiest to obtain would be the Flaming Mace (craftable from a Mace, which can be found in Gold Chests located underground).
Tendon Bow is an easily obtainable and powerful bow at this stage.
You can combine them with either Unholy Arrows or Jester's Arrows, which greatly help to kill the swarm of Creepers.
The Crimson Rod is a great support weapon that can easily be obtained through Crimson Hearts.
A Diamond Staff is very good at taking out the Creepers because of its high fire rate, large hitbox and pierce.
If the Snapthorn is too difficult to obtain, one can use the Vasculash, which is a weaker alternative.
The summon tag icon will linger on the correct Brain, which may be helpful in identifying the correct copy.

summon.text: Deerclops can be summoned manually by using a Deer Thing in the Snow or Ice biome, at any time.

prepChecklist.text: Clear a large flat area in the Snow biome
Set your spawn point away from where Deerclops can wander
Drink a Warmth Potion: its buff cuts Deerclops's damage by 30%
Equip a Hand Warmer against the Frozen debuff
Drink Ironskin, Endurance and Regeneration Potions
Drink a Swiftness Potion to help dodge
Equip a Cloud in a Bottle (or a better jump accessory)
Carry a stack of the best healing potion you have

strategies.text: Avoid lingering directly above Deerclops, as the Shadow Hands it summons in this situation are very dangerous.
The player can run between Deerclops's legs without taking damage. This is useful for avoiding the first two Ice Spike attacks, but the player should not stick around for the third.

If it is close to the player, Deerclops will smash the ground, summoning a wave of Ice Spikes that quickly travels towards the player. Every third consecutive wave does not go as far, instead spreading in both directions.

If the player is more than 30 tiles away, Deerclops will turn a dark shade of purple, two reddish, semi-transparent images of Deerclops will begin spinning around it, and it becomes immune to all damage.
Due to being able to inflict Slow from a large range, accessories like the Anklet of the Wind or Magiluminescence alongside Swiftness Potions can help make the fight much more manageable.
The Frozen debuff from the Ice Spike attack is capable of interrupting a player's extending grappling hook, causing them to drop to the ground.
Shadow Hands are summoned more frequently as Deerclops's life gets lower. Shadow Hands predict the player's movements.
The Flamarang can deal very high damage to Deerclops at a safer distance than most swords.
The Terragrim performs excellently if acquired, especially if you stand under Deerclops and swing up towards his torso.
The Demon or Tendon Bow can be used for players who find it hard to obtain other weapons.
The Musket or The Undertaker are decent and the Minishark can also be used.
The Vilethorn is a solid choice, especially due to Deerclops's low defense.
The Space Gun is a good weapon, especially when combined with Meteor armor.
Sentry weapons like the Ballista Rod and Explosive Trap Rod are more viable on Deerclops than other bosses due to it slow speed and large body.
The Snapthorn is the best whip when using most minions against Deerclops.

summon.text: Duke Fishron is summoned by fishing in the Ocean at any time, using a Truffle Worm as bait

The Eater of Worlds spawns upon destroying every third Shadow Orb in a Corruption world. It can also be summoned manually by using a Worm Food in The Corruption or Underground Corruption, at any time.

prepChecklist.text: Classic Mode: build a tall, thin surface arena that is easy to climb, with many platforms
Keep the arena low enough that the Corruption background stays visible
If breaking Shadow Orbs, prepare a quick, safe escape to your surface arena
Place a Bed next to the arena so you can teleport there
Hang an Eater of Souls Banner to reduce their damage
Drink Ironskin and Regeneration Potions
Drink a Hunter Potion to spot it while it burrows
Carry a stack of the best healing potion you have

strategies.text: Beware that, when a segment dies, the segments in front and behind will detach and separately attack the player.
To avoid getting overwhelmed by many worms at once, it may be helpful to only aim for the head or tail of the worm, as these segments will not cause the boss to split further when killed.
If you destroy a middle segment, concentrate on the smaller worm, since the larger one can be easy to predict and dodge.

Like other worm enemies, once the Eater's head passes a given point, every body segment must follow. This allows the player to stand next to the body, attacking every segment as it goes by. The player should be wary of the head looping back around.
In Classic Mode, Grenades are an effective weapon against the Eater. That is not true in higher difficulties, since the Eater gains resistance to explosives.
The Eater of Worlds will start to flee underground if the player leaves the Corruption biome, but will not immediately despawn.
Vile Spit is the Eater of Worlds' most dangerous attack, so it is important to bring sufficient mobility accessories and make an arena that enables you to dodge.
Broadswords do very well against this boss.
Spears such as the Swordfish can damage multiple segments at once, and are most effective if you try to line them up with the boss's length.
Jester's Arrows can pierce through infinitely many segments, although the damage drops each segment.
The Demon Bow is easily available and powerful.
The Vilethorn is good for spreading damage across the boss's entire body.
Topaz's small explosion is very helpful in this fight, shredding through segments of the boss.
The Flinx Staff is consistently available and can damage a lot of segments at once if spread out.
Pairing 1 Vampire Frog and 2 Flinx will grant the most DPS available for summoners.

summon.text: The Empress of Light is summoned by killing a Prismatic Lacewing, at any time. Prismatic Lacewings spawn in The Hallow on the Surface between dusk (7:30 PM) and midnight (12:00 AM) once Plantera has been defeated.
The Eye of Cthulhu can be summoned manually using a Suspicious Looking Eye at night (from 7:30 PM to 4:30 AM).

prepChecklist.text: Build a screen-sized arena with several rows of wooden platforms
Light the arena with Torches: the fight is at night
Place Campfires and Heart Lanterns in the arena for health regeneration
Summon it just after dusk (7:30 PM) for the most time before dawn
Drink Regeneration, Ironskin and Swiftness Potions
Wear Hermes Boots (or equivalents) to dodge the second phase's rams
Bring a Cloud in a Bottle (or equivalent) to avoid the rams
Carry a stack of the best healing potion you have

strategies.text: After spawning 3 or 4 Servants, the Eye will charge at you, attempting to ram you 3 times before hovering once more, so be prepared to evade.
It can be helpful to begin to evade after the 3rd servant is spawned, as this will often allow you to dodge its first charge.
The Servants are weak and can be killed for Hearts, or, if there is enough room, the player can simply keep moving in one direction to avoid them.
Make sure to take advantage of its transformation sequence as much as possible, since it just spins in place for a few moments and you can still damage it.
For the last half of the fight, the boss sheds its iris to reveal a fanged mouth. It moves slightly faster and deals more damage when it hits you, but it also has no defense.
With a wide enough arena, running in a straight line while the Eye of Cthulhu does his quick charge is fast enough to avoid any damage, and allows the player to attack continuously.
The boss looks at the player it will follow, which can be helpful information in multiplayer.
In the first phase of the fight it spawns more servants and enters the second phase at 65% health instead of 50%, spawning 4–5 more Servants in that process.
In this part of the fight, after the 3 normal lunges it will perform a brief series of extremely quick dashes at a steeper angle.
Long-range projectile swords can safely attack at a distance.
Yoyos have good range and allow for fine control.
Bows are easy to craft and do good damage.
Frostburn Arrows deal the most damage to the boss itself and inflict Frostburn, but Jester's Arrows can kill the Servants and hurt the Eye in the same shot.
The Wand of Frosting is relatively easy to obtain and inflicts the strong Frostburn debuff.
The Crimson Rod is an excellent side-weapon, as its clouds can be set up to clear out the servants while also dealing steady damage to the boss.
The Cobwhip is the easiest whip to obtain at this point in the game, although it is weaker than other options.
Two somewhat stronger options are Leather Whip, which can be bought from the Zoologist NPC, and the Slime Whip, which can be crafted at a Solidifier.

summon.text: Golem is summoned by using a Lihzahrd Power Cell at the Lihzahrd Altar located in the final chamber of the Jungle Temple, at any time, and only if the current world is in Hardmode after Plantera is defeated.
King Slime can be summoned by using the Slime Crown, in any biome at any time.

prepChecklist.text: Build one or two long rows of platforms above the ground
Place Campfires and Heart Lanterns in the arena for health regeneration
Hang a Blue Slime Banner for its offensive and defensive buffs
Bring a long-range weapon to keep a safe distance from his contact damage
Drink Ironskin and Regeneration Potions
Drink a Swiftness Potion for mobility
Equip a double-jump accessory such as a Cloud in a Bottle
Carry a stack of the best healing potion you have

strategies.text: The pattern of his jumps is predictable and repeatedly: two normal, one small, and one high.
After the high jump, the King Slime can teleport to the player.
When King Slime is about to teleport, he shrinks, and his map icon will get closer to the ground.
Getting too far away from King Slime will make it teleport to the player, meaning that the player cannot escape by simply running offscreen.
King Slime becomes smaller and faster the lower his health is, which makes him harder to hit.
Piercing weapons can not only damage King Slime, but also kill the additional slimes he spawns.
If he or his slimes reach the platform, drop down temporarily and use hooks or double-jumps to return; this will cause King Slime and his minions to drop down as well, following you.
King Slime is very slow in liquids.
However, when damaged it will spawn Spiked Slimes in addition to regular Blue Slimes.
The Thorn Chakram is a good option to keep the boss at range, but can struggle against the hordes of slimes.
The Ice Blade is a weaker option that is easier to obtain.
A cheap and powerful option is a bow, such as the Gold, Platinum, or even the Tendon/Demon Bow.
Frostburn Arrows or Jester's Arrows are the preferred ammo types, due to the high single target damage of the former and the piercing effect of the latter.
The Emerald Staff and all stronger staves do well against King Slime.
The Wand of Frosting is an easily obtained magic weapon that does well in this fight.
The best multiple-use summon weapons at this part of the game are the Flinx Staff and the Vampire Frog Staff.
The Soulscourge and Vasculash are weaker yet easier to obtain alternatives, only requiring mining Demonite or Crimtane.

summon.text: The Lunatic Cultist is summoned after killing the Cultists that spawn at the Dungeon's entrance after Skeletron and Golem have been defeated.
The Moon Lord will spawn after destroying the four Celestial Pillars or can be summoned manually using a Celestial Sigil in any world where Golem has been defeated.

After all three mechanical bosses have been defeated, Plantera's Bulbs will randomly spawn in the Underground Jungle (indicated by the status message "The jungle grows restless..."). These bulbs emit a faint pink light in dark areas and immediately summon Plantera nearby upon being destroyed, usually a fair distance off-screen.

The Queen Bee spawns upon breaking a Larva found inside Bee Hives in the Underground Jungle. She can also be summoned manually by using an Abeemination in the Jungle or Underground Jungle, at any time.

prepChecklist.text: Fight in a Hive: it is already carved out and its honey pool regenerates health
Stay in the Underground Jungle: outside it she enrages
Place Wood Platforms about every 5 blocks
Clear Larvae near the arena so you don't summon a second Queen Bee
Equip a Bezoar to remove the Poisoned debuff
Drink Ironskin, Endurance and Regeneration Potions
Drink a Swiftness Potion to help dodge
Craft Bottled Honey from the Hive's honey

strategies.text: When she charges you, use platforms and/or a double jump or better to dodge upwards.
When she summons her Bees, use a weapon that can pierce targets and aim for her tail to stop the Bees the moment they spawn.
If any Bees manage to escape then use a sword with a large swing to clear them out.
If she's using the stinger-shooting phase, keep moving back and forth.
Getting hit by a stinger inflicts a Poisoned debuff that will last longer than running into Queen Bee, so make sure to dodge it.
Solid blocks can help to block the stingers.
Queen Bee is one of the few bosses that does not despawn when the player teleports away.
As the Queen Bee's health goes down, she will become a lot more aggressive, shooting more stingers and having much faster charges.
Successfully dashing into an enemy gives the player brief invincibility frames, so if timed right, the charge attacks can be completely neutralized.
Swords can be surprisingly effective, doing the most damage when the Queen Bee is releasing Bees or when charging you.
The Thorn Chakram, Trimarang, or Flamarang are good at killing the Queen Bee, due to their long range.
Bring along arrows that can pierce, such as Jester's Arrows or Unholy Arrows.
Note that the Minishark is much less effective in Expert Mode, especially in the latter stages of the battle, unless paired with the Shark Tooth Necklace.
Amethyst's homing ability is very helpful in this fight, being able to track the boss when she's dashing.
The Space Gun is a good weapon, especially when combined with Meteor armor. Its piercing effect will help with taking out the Bees.
Summoners should use the Flinx Staff or, preferably, the Vampire Frog Staff, together with one of the early whips.

summon.text: Queen Slime is summoned by using a Gelatin Crystal in The Hallow or Underground Hallow, at any time.

Summoning Skeletron requires the player to speak to the Old Man at the Dungeon's entrance at night. Upon selecting the "Curse" option, he will turn into Skeletron. Skeletron can only be summoned once per night, as the Old Man will not respawn until dawn. Once Skeletron is defeated, the Old Man's curse will be lifted and he will no longer appear. Skeletron will thereafter only be summonable with the Clothier Voodoo Doll. Killing the Clothier at night with this accessory equipped will summon Skeletron.

prepChecklist.text: Plan the arena above the Dungeon roof or beside the Dungeon
Leave the Dungeon floor intact: edits there can stop the Cultists spawning later
Leave room to dodge the hands and vertical space for the head spin
Start early in the night: it enrages if not defeated by 4:30 AM
Drink Ironskin, Endurance and Regeneration Potions
Drink a Swiftness Potion to outrun the spinning attack
Drink a Featherfall Potion for air mobility
Bring a grappling hook to escape the head-spin attack

strategies.text: Attacking the hands first is advised, as destroying them both will make it very easy to dodge Skeletron for the rest of the battle. This is pretty much mandatory in Expert Mode, as Skeletron gains 25 defense for each hand it has alive.
Timing is key in order to defend from the hands: after dodging them, use piercing weapons to deal damage to both arms (and Skeletron's skull, if it happens to align with them).
Try to avoid staying above or far to one side of Skeletron for a long time.

After some time, Skeletron will use its spinning attack. Skeletron moves slowly, but they constantly follow the player. During this attack, Skeletron's defense is lowered to zero, but gains more attack. The player should use the fastest weapon at their disposal to deal a lot of damage. However, make sure to constantly move; if the player gets hit by it, they might get stunlocked and take a lot of damage.
Skulls are blocked by solid blocks, so a barrier between the player and Skeletron can let the player attack Skeletron using a yoyo with impunity.
In Expert Mode, if the player keeps moving in different directions, most of the homing skulls will miss.
During the fight, use your platforms to move in circles around Skeletron, flying over and around him and running underneath.
Yoyos such as Amazon are excellent against Skeletron, as they can deal high damage from a distance.
Flails can work due to their long range and ability to hit both the arms and head with a single attack.
The Demon and Tendon Bow are the most accessible bows at this stage. Use them with Frostburn Arrows and Jester's Arrows.
Bone Javelins are very effective due to their high damage and firing speed.
Amethyst's homing ability is very helpful in this fight, being able to track the boss while the player focuses on dodging.
The Crimson Rod is also a very effective method of damaging Skeletron, even allowing it to be used in combination with other weapons.
The Vampire Frog Staff, from the Blood Moon, and Imp Staff, from the Underworld, are the strongest minions available.
The strongest sentry available is Houndius Shootius. The Ballista Rod or Flameburst Rod are also helpful alternatives.

summon.text: Skeletron Prime can be summoned manually using a Mechanical Skull at night (from 7:30 PM to 4:30 AM).
The Destroyer can be summoned manually using a Mechanical Worm at night (from 7:30 PM to 4:30 AM).
The Twins can be summoned manually using a Mechanical Eye at night (from 7:30 PM to 4:30 AM).
The Wall of Flesh can be summoned by dropping a Guide Voodoo Doll into lava in The Underworld while the Guide is alive, which destroys the Guide Voodoo Doll and kills the Guide in the process.
